target_customer: Governments, ministries of health and global health funders in developing countries
problem: Public health and emergency data sits in disconnected systems, so governments cannot analyze it quickly. Zenysis integrates the data into one analysis workspace (Harmony).
business_model: Enterprise and government software and services
product_category: Data integration and analytics for public health

founders.name: Jonathan Stambolis
founders.background_notes: Press describes him as co-founder and CEO who started the company in 2016 to help developing countries respond to emergencies and improve public health.

founders.name: Ian Webster
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder/CTO on the YC page; no bio.

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating messy, siloed government datasets in low-connectivity settings and building analysis tools on top is hard for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Government and global health partnerships and integrated data create switching costs, but sales cycles and funding depend on donors and ministries.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found. Commentary describes DHIS2 as a data source that Zenysis layers over, and Palantir later moved into public health; both are from undated or later sources.

market_need_then: Not documented by a source dated near 2016; later the Global Fund partnered with Zenysis in 2018 to advance data use in 10 countries fighting AIDS, tuberculosis and malaria.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission-driven; site tagline reads Data-Driven Insight. Human-Focused Impact.

brand_strength.rationale: A distinctive invented name but no press about the brand itself; recognition comes through global health partners.

outcome_analysis: Zenysis raised a reported seed in 2016, a Series A in 2018 and a $13.3M Series B in June 2022 led by the Steele Foundation for Hope, while partnering with the Global Fund from 2018. It remains active with about 11 people on the YC profile. Its customers are governments and funders, which gives it mission traction but a slow, donor-linked sales motion; no acquisition or layoff news was found.
notes: Seed (2.8M, 2016) and Series A (5.8M, 2018) amounts are stated by an outlet repeating them in 2022 coverage, with several trackers agreeing on Series A; investors for those rounds conflict (Employbl lists Tencent, Y Combinator, NKM Capital; others list Founders Fund, 500 Global), so left blank. Techloy alone names Peter Thiel and 500 Startups in the Series B. Totals range $13.3M to $22.7M. Founding year is unclear: CB Insights says 2015, press says 2016. Company site and YC page give no founder education or prior employers beyond the press note on Stambolis. No competitor sourced to 2016 was found.
